title: He Survived 3 Days at the Bottom of the Atlantic. Then a Diver Reached for a "Body"
description: Case 001, the full case file. On 26 May 2013 the tugboat Jascon-4 capsized off Nigeria and sank about 30 metres. The cook, Harrison Okene, found a pocket of air and stayed alive in the dark for about 60 hours, until divers sent to recover bodies found a hand that grabbed back. Rook, Survra's sceptical crow detective, checks the story from the locked cabin doors to the decompression chamber.
source_notes: Sources differ on details: AP reports one bottle of Coke, ABC reports six sodas; time underwater is given as 60 to 62 hours (one report says 72). Script uses 'one bottle of Coke' (AP/BBC) and 'sixty hours'. Long version adds: locked cabins as an anti-piracy routine, the mattress platform, the life vest with two flashlights, the plank, the hammer, hot water and breathing mask, more than two days of decompression and the stars (Fox/Reuters/The Nation, NBC/LiveScience, AP via Gulf News). Time underwater is reported as about 60 hours by most outlets and 72 by some; the script says 'about sixty'.

quality_gate.method: automated gate (pacing, motion, repetition, loudness, host presence, originality) plus still-frame review; audio was measured, not listened to
